newsitem.title: BULGARIA: IMF ASKS BULGARIA PARLT TO DISCUSS CURRENCY BOARD.
newsitem.headline: IMF ASKS BULGARIA PARLT TO DISCUSS CURRENCY BOARD.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) asked Bulgaria's parliament to begin discussions on introducing a currency board system, state radio said on Tuesday.

"The Deputy Director of the IMF European Department, Michael Deppler, asked the speaker of the Bulgarian Parliament, Blagovest Sendov, to begin discussions with the political parties on the issue of introducing a currency board system," the radio said.
It said Sendov had said that the currency board should be introduced through legislation.
On Monday the IMF urged Bulgarian authorities to adopt special measures involving serious restrictions on foreign currency trade in a bid to restore credibility in the slumping national currency.
Deppler met with President Zhelyu Zhelev, senior government and central bank officials as part of an IMF mission visit in Sofia to agree on reform policies that would release further funding.

The IMF has twice so far postponed a $115 million loan due to Bulgaria's failure to meet reform targets which include curbing inflation, stabilising the exchange rate, speeding up privatisation and closing loss-making enterprises.
Deppler said that Bulgaria's problems were much bigger and deeper than the Fund or the government had thought they would be.
Delayed structural reforms and a stagnant economy have pressured the lev to 249 to the dollar on Tuesday from around 70 in January.

Under a currency board system introduced in some parts of the world to boost credibility in their national currencies, the amount of national currency in circulation must be exactly matched by the central bank's hard currency reserves.
But it also deprives the bank of the usual tools of monetary management, such as market interventions and interest rates.
In a bid to stabilise the lev, Bulgaria's central bank raised the central interest rate to a record-high 300 percent in September. It is currently 180 percent.
The government has delayed drafting the budget frame for next year due to unpredictability of the interest rate.
